phenotype: DEL. Originally identified by Singleton et al. 2001 as one of the first molecular causes of the Del phenotype (Japanese collaboration, Okubo group). ORIGIN OF THE ALLELE: Flegel and Srivastava 2024 (Transfusion 64:1187-1190) place this variant among the first four RHD alleles ever recognised as molecular causes of the Del phenotype, attributing it to Singleton BK, Green CA, Kimura K, Minami A, Okubo Y, Daniels GL. Two new RHD mutations associated with the Del phenotype. Transfus Clin Biol 2001;8(Suppl 1) - a conference abstract, which is why the variant is absent from PubMed and ClinVar searches by nucleotide string. The other three founding DEL alleles were RHD(K409K) (c.1227G>A, the Asian-type DEL), RHD(IVS3+1G>A) and RHD(M295I), the latter three from Wagner et al. 2001. Raud et al., 2019 illustrate Minigene analysis consistent with serology from other studies. INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION: McGowan et al. 2024 detected the allele in an Australian blood donor (sample 8) on reanalysis after splice sites were added to their exome pipeline. PREDICTION: AlphaGenome splicing 2.57 and SpliceAI 0.99, both maximal-range calls; AlphaGenome RNA-seq -3.53, among the largest predicted expression reductions in the dataset. NOT covered by the Fichou et al. 2015 minigene panel, which did not include any intron 1 variant.

c.149-2632T>A is a deep intronic change in intron 1, reported in one patient with a very weak D phenotype (Floch et al. 2022, Transfusion 62:E14-E16). CONFIRMED FROM THE PRIMARY TEXT (Results, 7 Sep 2026). Serology: RBCs typed D-negative by immediate spin but weakly positive (1+ to 2+) by indirect antiglobulin test with all anti-D tested; monoclonal anti-D in the RhD Variant Investigation Kit were reactive at 1+ to 2+ except LHM174/102 and LDM1, which were non-reactive; C+E-c+e+ with no reduced reactivity; direct antiglobulin test negative. Genetics: the sample was hemizygous for RHD, and exon-specific amplification and sequencing of RHD, RHCE and RHAG found no changes from conventional. Mechanism: RHD cDNA analysis from the patient found ONLY transcripts carrying an 80-bp intron 1 sequence inserted between the exon 1 and exon 2 sequences (RHD c.149-2624_2704, i.e. 2624-2704 bp upstream of exon 2) - a pseudo-exon inclusion. The T>A change lies 9 bp into that insert and likely promotes the aberrant splice site; it was confirmed by amplification and Sanger sequencing of 370 bp of RHD intron 1 from genomic DNA. The resulting transcript contains a premature stop codon 30-32 bp into the insert. Evidence is therefore patient-derived transcript characterisation in a single case, with NO heterologous functional assay (no minigene or reporter), which meets neither Tier 1 route. Absent from gnomAD v4. AlphaGenome splicing 0.966; SpliceAI 0.14.

phenotype: Wild type. Normal D antigen expression from the allele carrying c.1154-31T>C. In the Rui et al. 2023 index donor, genotype RHD(c.845G>A)/RHD(c.149-29G>C, c.1154-31T>C) typed 4+ by gel and 3+ by tube with human monoclonal anti-D; the weak D phenotype was attributable to c.845G>A on the other allele, while the allele carrying c.1154-31T>C encoded normal D antigen.
molecular_mechanism: The reference base at c.1154-31 is T, so the correct notation is c.1154-31T>C. Rui et al. 2023 established this from the locus reference genomic sequence NG_007494.1 for RHD blood group alleles, finding T rather than C at this locus, and noted that other authors had already presented the variation as c.1154-31T>C. The ISBT designation RHD*01EL.37, which lists the variant as c.1154-31C>T among the alleles held responsible for DEL phenotypes, therefore rests on an inverted reference orientation. Several independent lines of evidence show no effect on D antigen expression from this position alone. Fichou et al. 2015 carried out extensive functional analyses of RHD splice site variants and found that c.1154-31T>C alone had no functional impact on splicing, with no documented phenotype. Costes et al. 2017 found by next generation sequencing that the variant is always associated in cis with the missense mutation c.1154G>C on the RHD weak type 2 allele and is in linkage disequilibrium with it, that it can be found alone on the RHD gene as a neutral polymorphism, and that the independent site demonstrates a neutral effect on phenotype whether it carries C or T. Bub et al. 2017 associated weak D expression with c.1154G>C, c.1154-8T>A and c.1154-31T>C acting together rather than with the intronic change by itself. In the index case of Rui et al. 2023, a donor with the genotype RHD(c.845G>A)/RHD(c.149-29G>C, c.1154-31T>C) typed 4+ by gel and 3+ by tube with human monoclonal anti-D, confirmed by family study and PacBio sequencing; the weak D antigen was encoded by c.845G>A on one allele while the allele carrying c.1154-31T>C encoded normal D antigen. The population frequency is out of proportion to the phenotype, at 22.3% by the LOVD3 platform (2577 of 11562) against a DEL phenotype frequency of roughly 0.15% in East Asian populations. The parallel case of c.149-29G>C, formerly RHD*01EL.32, was similarly shown not to cause a DEL phenotype by Kim et al. 2021.

The same study screened 13 weak D, DEL or D-negative samples with normal RHD exons; GATA1 motifs were intact in 12 of 13 and rs675072 was not the cause in any of them. The one variant attributable to a phenotype was a different change, c.1-110A>C, in a DEL sample.

molecular_mechanism: RHD c.148+2delT (IVS1+2delT) deletes the T of the canonical GT donor dinucleotide of intron 1. RHeference (RHef00722) records one sample from donors pooled for RHD DNA analysis in the Swiss population, citing von Arx et al. 2019 (Vox Sang abstract, 'A novel RHD splice donor site mutation leading to a RhD-negative phenotype'). The primary abstract could not be found, and the available description of the Swiss case appears to refer to a c.148+1 substitution (148+1T) rather than this deletion, so the serological case cannot be confirmed for c.148+2delT. No in-vitro assay has been reported. Absent from dbSNP and gnomAD v4. In-silico tools predict a strong effect (AlphaGenome RNA-seq -3.35, AlphaGenome splicing 2.50, SpliceAI 0.99).
